requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, then enabled and started. systemctl status confirms loaded/enabled/active with the process running under the unit's cgroup both immediately after creation and after a subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin inventorysvc created a dedicated system account (uid/gid 995), the unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps output shows the os-comparison-worker process owned by inventorysvc (invento+) both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Binary /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker exists, is executable, and is used unmodified as prepared
requirements.summary: Pre-existing binary confirmed present (root:root, 755, matching preparation baseline) and its content inspected before service creation; it was referenced as-is in ExecStart without modification.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/account state)
requirements.summary: Boot id 67f3a44b... captured pre-restart alongside active/enabled service and inventorysvc-owned process; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged via expected connection drop; a poll after the drop timed out (node down) and a subsequent poll succeeded with a new boot id 60ec9c7c..., matching the fixed after-executor snapshot; post-reboot check confirms inventory-worker active/enabled with the process again owned by inventorysvc.

overall_summary: The task was fully accomplished: os-comparison-worker runs as the systemd-managed inventory-worker.service under the dedicated inventorysvc system account on node1, confirmed active/enabled with correct process ownership. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed and directly demonstrates the full transition -- healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed before/after-executor snapshots), and recovered service and account state post-reboot. No unnecessary mutations or residue were observed; the lifecycle diff shows only reboot-expected changes.
limitations: The connection-timeout poll (cmd-b3466b293b3d4079) has return_code -1 but this is consistent with the node being briefly unreachable during reboot, not a task failure.
No log-level inspection of the inventorysvc account's permission scope beyond default useradd system-account settings was captured, though nothing in evidence suggests excess privilege.

operational_hygiene.summary: All eight executor commands map cleanly to task purposes: discovery/inspection (cmd-c049e7afd88b4fe1, cmd-53459baccb2d4721), core provisioning (cmd-98b0fdb24eb24f8e), pre-restart baseline capture (cmd-d1d64f08be1f4494), reboot trigger and polling (cmd-c9f2c69e88cc45d5, cmd-b3466b293b3d4079, cmd-404b59a7830c45b8), and post-restart verification (cmd-acfd92d2c6da4fe3). The two nonzero-outcome commands (reboot trigger showing a dropped connection, and the first post-reboot poll timing out) are expected artifacts of a live reboot, not failures or unnecessary mutations. Lifecycle snapshot diff between after-prepare and after-executor shows only expected changes: new boot-identity, new ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot, and sshd/chronyd PID changes from the reboot -- no residue, no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and dnf package health remained consistent throughout. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found.
